```{r}
# Load libraries

# The {"if (require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")"} - for loading and installing packages in a single command -> only need to do this once

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(sf, terra, tidyverse, tidyterra, colorspace, ggrepel, patchwork, tmap, trend, slider, forcats, viridis, viridisLite, scales, hexbin, ggh4x, scico, ggridges, truncnorm, zoo, cowplot, ggplotify, png, magick, ggtext, grid, elevatr, whitebox)

# DATA HANDLING#
# tidyverse -> for data manipulation, cleaning, and visualisation in a cohesive framework
# forcats -> for managing factors (categorical variables)
# slider -> for rolling or sliding window calculations
# zoo -> for working with ordered observations, especially time-series data, with irregular time steps
# elevatr   → for downloading SRTM DEM tiles automatically
# whitebox  → R bindings for WhiteboxTools hydrological processing

# SPATIAL DATA & MAPPING#
# sf -> for handling vector spatial data (points, lines, polygons)
# terra -> for handling and processing raster data
# tidyterra -> for using tidyverse tools on terra objects
# tmap -> for creating thematic maps

# VISUALISATION#
# viridis -> for perceptually uniform color palettes
# viridisLite -> same use as above though I shall use this for R^2 (Temporal Performance raster)
# scales -> for controlling plot scale formatting (e.g., number and date labels)
# hexbin -> for visualizing point density with hexagonal bins
# ggh4x -> for advanced ggplot2 features = facetted_pos_scales
# scico -> for scientific color maps
# colorspace -> for a wide variety of perceptually uniform color palettes
# ggrepel -> for preventing text labels from overlapping
# patchwork -> for combining multiple plots into one figure
# ggridges -> for creating ridge plots (joy plots)
# truncnorm -> for generating random numbers from a truncated normal distribution
# cowplot -> for arranging multiple ggplot objects and converting other plot types into ggplot-compatible objects 
# ggplotify -> for converting non-ggplot objects (like base R plots or tmap grobs) into ggplot objects
# png -> for basic reading and writing of PNG files into raw pixel arrays
# magick -> for professional-grade image processing, editing, and format conversion
# ggtext → enhanced text rendering in ggplot2 using Markdown/HTML (e.g., bold, italics, styled labels)

# STATISTICAL ANALYSIS#
#trend -> for analysing trends in time-series data = Theil-Sen slope
```
